title: Geo provisioning orchestration spec and sales handback guide
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Objective: Define a pragmatic orchestration specification and a repeatable sales handback guide for enterprise region/data-residency requests (new region provisioning, failover enablement, and strict residency constraints). This doc ties eligibility checks, cost estimation, provisioning runway, expected lead times, and a clear handoff checklist for Sales/SEs into a single pipeline that can be operationalized by PM, Solutions, and Infra teams.

Context: Customers increasingly ask for region-specific availability for compliance, latency, and contractual residency. Current intake is ad-hoc: Sales submits email threads, Infra does ad-hoc sizing, and PMs coordinate case-by-case. That creates long lead times and inconsistent contractual language. We need a spec that: 1) standardizes decision gates (eligibility, risk, capacity), 2) produces a fast, defensible cost and timeline estimate, and 3) provides Sales with a one-page handback and clear escalation triggers.

Scope: New public region onboard requests and enterprise-only private residency (VPC/on-prem) requests tied to contractual SLAs. Excludes routine failover testing for existing region pairs (that will be covered by a separate runbook).
acceptance_criteria: A1: A documented orchestration spec exists that lists eligibility gates, required inputs, and outputs for each stage (scoping -> sizing -> KT -> contract language).
A2: Sales handback template (one-pager) created and validated by Solutions and Legal with placeholders for SLA commitments, lead time, and cost estimate.
A3: Automated cost-estimate spreadsheet + sample sizing configs for common request patterns (single-region read-only residency, full-residency with failover).
A4: Triage play integrated into intake form so requests render recommended next steps and priority score for PM review.
A5: Clear escalation matrix documented with point owners and SLA for responses (48h initial triage, 10 business days for firm estimate).
steps: Step 0: Intake capture - Sales/Customer completes canonical Geo Provisioning Intake form (fields: customer ARR, required region(s), data residency level, regulatory citations, expected traffic and latency SLOs, contract deadline).
Step 1: Auto-score - Intake system computes eligibility score (priority band) using rules: ARR threshold, legal/regulatory flag, customer tier, and latency/geography constraints.
Step 2: PM scoping - PM owner reviews packet, flags blockers (security, export controls), and assigns to Infra/Capacity/Network as needed.
Step 3: Quick cost & timeline - Infra provides 3-tier estimate (conservative, typical, accelerated) with cost delta and lead times.
Step 4: Compliance & legal review - If residency requires contractual changes or SOC/ISO attestations, Legal is engaged and a baseline clause is drafted.
Step 5: Provisioning runbook creation - Infra writes region provisioning runbook with environment templates, expected GCP/Azure/AWS region mapping, and test plan.
Step 6: Sales handback - PM produces one-pager with final estimate, lead time, required contract language, and post-provisioning acceptance criteria.
Step 7: Handoff & commit - Sales/Customer signs ahead-of-time commitment (if required) and Ops schedules provisioning window.
Step 8: Post-provision acceptance - Run acceptance tests (latency, residency verification, failover simulation) and close the ticket.
risks: R1: Underestimated lead times leading to missed contractual SLAs.
R2: Hidden regulatory constraints requiring longer legal review (e.g., cross-border transfer permissions).
R3: Capacity exhaustion in target region that requires cross-region fallback and increases cost.
R4: Misaligned expectations between Sales and Infra on what "data residency" guarantees (logical vs physical segregation).
R5: Automation gaps - manual runbook steps increase execution variability.

progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Kickoff with Infra, Solutions, Legal. Collected sample intake from three prospective enterprise customers. Assigned Marco as capacity lead.
2025-11-09: Completed first-pass scoring rules; built prototype of auto-score in Google Sheet. Seeking feedback from Sales on weightings.
2025-11-12: Legal reviewed draft one-pager; requested explicit language for cross-border processing and audit rights. Added Legal as mandatory reviewer for high-risk flags.
2025-11-18: Infra provided conservative/typical/accelerated lead time matrix for 6 common region flavors. Drafted Sales handback template; seeking Solutions review this week.
escalation_matrix: Trigger A (legal/regulatory block): Escalate to Legal (Omar Rahman) within 24h, PM owner to inform Director of Product.
Trigger B (capacity shortage): Infra on-call (Marco Diaz) to propose fallback within 48h and notify Sales.
Trigger C (timeline slip >20%): PM to open triage with GTM leadership and propose contract amendment or customer credit.
notes: Design decision: Tiered estimate model chosen to avoid committing to fixed pricing pre-capacity confirmation.
Follow-up: Build intake form validation to require regulatory citation when customer checks 'regulatory residency' flag.
Open question: Should we require minimum ARR for firm SLA commitments? Initial recommended cutoff: $250k ARR but needs GTM alignment.
